mathematical_review: Original-graph conflict semantics and arbitrary candidate sets are retained throughout.
Cover identities, triangle losses, preliminary subcubic bounds, and root-type incidence counts were checked.
Double-tip saturation, unique-triple and outer-edge bounds were checked, including the threshold-free expository variants explained in Appendix A.
The subcubic eighteen-edge exclusion, weighted seventeen-edge defect calculation, thirteen-vertex support bound, and both remaining defect configurations were checked.
The five strengthened thresholds are proved in dependency order: high20, high21, high22, high23, and high24.
Twenty-clique rigidity identifies the full edge set of an actual original-graph doubled-five-cycle connected component.
The private-neighbourhood exchange and count use degrees in the candidate conflict graph and transfer the original-graph thresholds in the correct direction.
The final component removal preserves the original graph, counts actual components, and yields 2|F| <= 39|M| + t_G(F).
The pure 19.5 specialization and necessity of the correction are stated separately, and no weighted or colouring conclusion is inferred.
